assumptions.text: The open decision OD-1 about screening outage behaviour is resolved as described in notes/analysis_notes.md: on a screening outage the quote is refused with status `refused_screening`, so that no price reaches an unscreened shipper.

On a screening outage (ScreeningUnavailableError), a refusal notice is still attempted to be sent via NotificationService.send_refusal_notice, and any failure in that notification is ignored as fire-and-forget, same as for refusal decisions with a risk index.
Failures in QuoteStore.update_quote are treated as generic unexpected errors and are allowed to raise, since no behaviour is specified for them in the documents.
The QuoteStore.store_draft method returns a string quote_id on success and raises StoreUnavailableError on storage failure; no other return shapes are used.
The ScreeningService.screen method returns an integer risk_index on success and raises ScreeningUnavailableError on outage; no other error signalling is used.

NotificationService.send_quote_document and NotificationService.send_refusal_notice may raise exceptions to signal delivery failure; all such exceptions must be swallowed so that response and stored outcome remain unchanged.

claims.text: Validation DT-V defines the request as valid iff all four field rules hold; otherwise the request is rejected immediately with status `rejected: invalid_request` and no draft is stored, no screening is performed, no price is computed, and no notification is sent.
On storage failure nothing else runs: no screening call, no pricing, no notification; status `error: store_unavailable`.

Flow order is: validate, store draft with status draft, request risk index, apply screening decision DT-S and update stored quote to resulting status, price DT-P only on priced rows, notify shipper only on notified rows, then return response.

DT-S defines three bands: risk_index <= 41 leads to status `quoted`, priced yes, notified with quote document; 42 <= risk_index <= 66 leads to status `review_hold`, priced no, notified no; risk_index >= 67 leads to status `refused_screening`, priced no, notified with refusal notice.
On DT-S review row, no price is computed and no notification is sent.
On DT-S refuse row, pricing never runs and refusal is notified; notification is fire-and-forget.
Notification is fire-and-forget: a delivery failure never changes the stored quote or the response.
DT-P pricing rules: base = 0.87 * weight_kg + 1.13 * distance_km; if weight_kg > 1244 add 316.00; if distance_km >= 4912 multiply running total by 1.19 after P2; final price is round(result, 2).
Long-haul multiplier for distance_km >= 4912 is applied after the heavy surcharge step P2; the order is normative.
API response must contain status and includes quote_id whenever a draft was stored, and price exactly on priced rows (i.e., only when status is quoted).
